primary.purpose: The one filled action, the focus ring, the mark that says you are here, and one whole wall. --palette-saffron in the code.

primary-dark.purpose: The filled action on hover and press. --palette-saffron-deep in the code.

on-primary.purpose: The words on the filled action. --palette-ink in the code.

dusk-deep.purpose: The header, the footer, the phone menu, the walk's cue, the pill the stop marks stand on.

limewash.purpose: Words on dusk; the ground of reading sections; white paint: a fringe, a rim, a sample's tag, a town or a number on a painted plaque.

ink.purpose: Words on saffron and on limewash.

ink-on-saffron.purpose: Secondary words on the saffron section.

haze.purpose: Secondary words on dusk and deep dusk.

coral.purpose: The sign painter's hard shade under the headline and the tagline. Never words.

enamel.purpose: A plaque's plate; the walk's card; a stop's name.

line.purpose: The line between rows on dusk: limewash at 20%.

line-strong.purpose: A field's edge and a quiet button's on dusk: limewash at 55%.

line-on-saffron.purpose: The line between rows on saffron: ink at 22%.

line-on-limewash.purpose: The line between rows on limewash: ink at 16%.

line-strong-on-light.purpose: The line that opens a list on saffron and on limewash: ink at 55%.

tin-shade.purpose: The grooves between a drawn roof's ribs.

steel-deep.purpose: The gaps between the slats; the shutter's bottom rail.

pavement.purpose: The kerb under a drawn shopfront and under the 404's empty plot.

roomlight.purpose: A lamp's bloom on the street plate; the light in a doorway where no room is painted. Sampled from a painted plate. Never text.

ground-lepalatier.purpose: Its sign board: paint on a plate, flat on its sign plates.

ground-lepalatier-ink.purpose: Its lettering: the one value the code sets on its painted board.

ground-lepalatier-accent.purpose: Its trim: a paint on its page, the rule on its strategy's cover.

ground-lepalatier-wall.purpose: The colour its wall is painted; a paint on its page.

ground-lakrem.purpose: Its sign board: paint on a plate, flat on its sign plates.

ground-lakrem-ink.purpose: Its lettering: the one value the code sets on its painted board.

ground-lakrem-accent.purpose: Its trim: a paint on its page, the rule on its strategy's cover.

ground-lakrem-wall.purpose: The colour its wall is painted; a paint on its page.

ground-souffle.purpose: Its sign board: paint on a plate, flat on its sign plates.

ground-souffle-ink.purpose: Its lettering: the one value the code sets on its painted board.

ground-souffle-accent.purpose: Its trim: a paint on its page, the rule on its strategy's cover.

ground-souffle-wall.purpose: The colour its wall is painted; a paint on its page.

ground-bouke.purpose: Its sign board: paint on a plate, flat on its sign plates.

ground-bouke-ink.purpose: Its lettering: the one value the code sets on its painted board.

ground-bouke-accent.purpose: Its trim: a paint on its page, the rule on its strategy's cover.

ground-bouke-wall.purpose: The colour its wall is painted; a paint on its page.

ground-larout.purpose: Its sign board: paint on a plate, flat on its sign plates.

ground-larout-ink.purpose: Its lettering: the one value the code sets on its painted board.

ground-larout-accent.purpose: Its trim: a paint on its page, the rule on its strategy's cover.

ground-larout-wall.purpose: The colour its wall is painted; a paint on its page.

ground-kazprop.purpose: Its sign board: paint on a plate, flat on its sign plates.

ground-kazprop-ink.purpose: Its lettering: the one value the code sets on its painted board.

ground-kazprop-accent.purpose: Its trim: a paint on its page, the rule on its strategy's cover.

ground-kazprop-wall.purpose: The colour its wall is painted; a paint on its page.

heading-1.purpose: The home page's headline only: slanted capitals with the sign painter's coral shade.

heading-2.purpose: Every other page's first heading, section headings, the tagline, a step's number, a real price at the head of its listing.

heading-3.purpose: The heading on a walk card, the phone menu's links, a list's heading on a listing.

heading-5.purpose: A business's name under its shopfront, a step's title, the name in the mark.

title-1.purpose: The lede under a page's heading; a question.

title-2.purpose: A section's lede; a listing's line and idea.

title-3.purpose: Header links, field labels, a paint's name.

title-4.purpose: A real listing's price under its shopfront.

body-1.purpose: The first line of the failed message.

body-3.purpose: Running text, list rows, chips, footer links.

body-4.purpose: The agency's name in the credit.

button-md.purpose: Buttons and arrow links: only what can be pressed.

button-sm.purpose: The header's small buttons, the skip link, the walk's cue.

caption-1.purpose: A field's error; a note that must be read.

caption-2.purpose: A sector and a town, a sample's price, hints, small print.

caption-4.purpose: What is written on a plaque: a number, a status, a town, a stop's name.

heading-1-wide.purpose: Not a named style: heading-1 as the home page's first screen sets it from 900px wide, to the mock-up's measure, times the stage's fit.

title-1-wide.purpose: Not a named style: the home page's lede as its first screen sets it from 900px wide.

shadows.name: plaque-rim
shadows.purpose: A plaque's white rim: a 1.5px limewash line set 1px inside the enamel. An edge, not a cast shadow.

shadows.name: walk-card-rim
shadows.purpose: The same rim at the size of a notice, on the walk's card.

shadows.name: field-error-edge
shadows.purpose: Thickens the edge of an invalid field to 2px.

shadows.name: current-page-ring
shadows.purpose: On a pill that leads to the page the visitor is already on.

shadows.name: sign-shade-headline
shadows.purpose: A text-shadow: the sign painter's hard coral shade under the home page's headline (heading-1).

shadows.name: sign-shade
shadows.purpose: A text-shadow: the same shade as a utility, used once, on the tagline.

motion.name: ease-roll
motion.purpose: How a roller shutter moves: it starts heavy and settles. A shutter on a shopfront, and a heading rising out of its mask.

motion.name: dur-press
motion.purpose: A button squashing to 0.96; a chip to 0.97.

motion.name: dur-press-shop
motion.purpose: A shopfront scaling to 0.985 while pressed.

motion.name: dur-state
motion.purpose: Field, chip, a question's colour, a stop's name, the cue 200; button fill and edge, underlines, skip link 240; arrow 280; the current page's line, the menu button 300; the plus, a stop's mark 320.

motion.name: dur-menu
motion.purpose: The phone menu's links arriving in reading order.

motion.name: dur-word
motion.purpose: One word of the tagline lighting from 0.5 of the ink to full ink.

motion.name: dur-reveal
motion.purpose: A reveal: it rises 18px and fades in, once.

motion.name: dur-shutter
motion.purpose: A shutter rolling on a shopfront.

motion.name: dur-mask
motion.purpose: A masked heading coming up out of its clip.

motion.name: dur-stage
motion.purpose: The plates fading in over their still.

motion.name: dur-lamp
motion.purpose: A lamp coming on over the painted street: from nothing to 0.85, settling at 0.4. Once.

motion.name: walk-hold
motion.purpose: The stage rests at each stop for the first and last 22% of the way to the next.

motion.name: walk-dissolve
motion.purpose: Between two paintings: the one that leaves grows to 1.1 and fades out, the one that arrives grows from 0.93 and fades in.

motion.name: first-words-fit
motion.purpose: The steps the stage tries, each with and then without the second route, until the first words stand clear of the roofline and above the sky's floor.

motion.name: tagline-muted
motion.purpose: The tagline's muted words: limewash at 0.5 on dusk measures 3.77:1.

components.name: Filled button
components.description: The one filled action in a group: saffron with ink, a full pill at least 48px tall.

components.name: Quiet button

components.name: Arrow link
components.description: A route that is not the main action: words, a thin underline and a drawn arrow that moves 4px when pointed at.
components.html: How it works

components.name: Field
components.description: An input on dusk: a limewash edge, 12px corners, its label above; an error is said in words under it.
components.css: .ds-field-ground { background: var(--palette-dusk, #0e328f); padding: 1.5rem; max-width: 26rem; } .ds-field-label { display: block; color: var(--color-ink, #f7f7f8); font-family: var(--font-sans, Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; font-weight: 500; } .ds-field { box-sizing: border-box; width: 100%; min-height: 3rem; margin-top: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid var(--color-line-strong, color-mix(in srgb, #f7f7f8 55%, transparent)); border-radius: 0.75rem; background: var(--color-paper, #0e328f); color: var(--color-ink, #f7f7f8); caret-color: var(--color-ink, #f7f7f8); padding: 0.75rem 1rem; font-family: var(--font-sans, Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; transition: border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-field:hover { border-color: var(--color-ink, #f7f7f8); } .ds-field:focus-visible { border-color: var(--color-ink, #f7f7f8); outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus, #f8c618); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-field[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--color-ink, #f7f7f8); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--color-ink, #f7f7f8); } .ds-field:disabled { border-color: var(--color-line, color-mix(in srgb, #f7f7f8 20%, transparent)); background: var(--color-paper-subtle, #082478); color: var(--color-ink-subtle, #b6c0db); cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Sample tag
components.description: What a sample wears across its shutter on every painting: white paint, ink capitals in the sign face, sized with the picture it hangs on. It cannot be pressed, and a sample's shutter never moves.

components.name: Stop marks
components.description: Where the walk is, and a way to jump along it: eight ticks on a solid pill of deep dusk at the foot of the stage. The current tick is taller and saffron; a tick pointed at grows and shows its stop's name on a small plaque above.
components.html: The streetThe signThe address

components.name: Drawn stand-in
components.description: A shopfront drawn in code, for a listing that has no painting: the same link, facts and rolling shutter as a painted shop. No page draws it today; all six listings are painted.

components.name: Walk card
components.description: A stop's words over the painted stage: a plaque at the size of a notice, solid enamel with a limewash rim, so its words never depend on the painting behind.
components.html:
The sign is already painted

A name chosen for the business, with its logo, colours and typefaces, ready to print and to post.
components.css: .ds-walk-card { box-sizing: border-box; max-width: 26rem; border-radius: 0.75rem; background: var(--color-plaque, #0b2b8e); color: var(--color-on-plaque, #f7f7f8); padding: 1.75rem; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 4px var(--color-plaque, #0b2b8e), inset 0 0 0 6px var(--color-on-plaque, #f7f7f8); } .ds-walk-card h2 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display, "Barlow Condensed", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: clamp(1.875rem, 1.7357rem + 0.5714vw, 2.25rem); line-height: 1.11; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.01em; text-wrap: balance; } .ds-walk-card p { margin: 0.75rem 0 0; font-family: var(--font-sans, Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; font-weight: 400; text-wrap: pretty; }

components.name: Lambrequin edge
components.description: Where one ground meets the next: a row of pierced scallops, 16px tall, in the colour of the ground above, hanging onto the ground below.
components.html: From the street to opening day

narrative.overview:
biznes.mu sells finished businesses in Mauritius, each built by Khay Digital and sold once, to one owner. Every business is a finished shopfront on one street at blue hour: its sign painted and lit, its shutter down. The street is painted. Five plates, generated illustrations in the style of the mock-up the owner approved, were each painted with every board, plaque, screen and paper left blank. What is true is set over the paint in code, from the data: a listing's own lettering on its board, its town or its number on its plaque, "Sample" on a sample's shutter.

The home page opens on that street and the scroll walks one shop, LePalatier, in eight stops: the street, the sign, the address, behind the shutter, the counter, the wall, the room, the whole street. Three beats: the street at dusk, behind the shutter, yours to open. Then the street as one terrace, the sale in four steps, the line said large, and the questions. A business's own page ends on one action: Ask about this business. Sold, it leaves the street.

The mood is a shop street after work, when the signs come on: saturated walls on a deep blue ground, lettering painted large, warm light where a room is open. One idea per block. Sections sit 64 to 128px apart, running text is held to 62ch, and a heading with its lede to 680px. Nothing in the palette or the type was invented: the interface's colours were measured from the mock-up the owner approved on 17 November 2026 (S1), the drawn stand-in's materials are region medians of the same picture (S2), two values were sampled from the plates themselves (S8, S9), and Barlow Condensed was matched to the mock-up's lettering by measurement (S3). What is derived says what it was derived from. Each listing's own colours and lettering are Khay Digital's direction (S6) and are content, not the platform's palette.
keyCharacteristics: `dusk` #0e328f is the page's ground and `limewash` #f7f7f8 its words (10.48:1); `dusk-deep` #082478 holds the header and the footer.
`primary` #f8c618, saffron, is the one filled action, the focus ring, the current page's line and one whole wall; on that wall the action turns `ink` #0a1639.
Barlow Condensed in capitals (`heading-1` to `heading-5`, `title-4`, `caption-4`) speaks whatever is painted on a sign; Geist carries every sentence.

The shopfront is the one picture of a business, and it is a painting: a tin roof, white fretwork, two lamps over a sign board, a roller shutter. Its lettering is the listing's own outline, set on the blank board in code.
The first words stand in the painted sky. They are shaped to the roofline, and their sentences are held above the afterglow, where white would not read.
The plaque, `enamel` #0b2b8e with a limewash rim (`rounded.plaque`, 6px), names what is fixed: a number, a status, a town. The walk's card is the same plaque at the size of a notice.
The lambrequin, a row of pierced scallops 16px tall, hangs where one ground meets the next.
Anything pressed is a full pill at least 48px tall (`button-primary`, `button-quiet`), 44px for the small button, a chip and the walk's cue.

The interface is flat; depth lives in the paintings. The stage moves each plate with one 2D transform, travels within a painting and dissolves on a push between two, and a still of itself stands wherever script does not run.

rules.name: The One Saffron Rule
rules.body: Saffron is a fill: the one filled action in a group, the focus ring, the mark that says "you are here", and one whole wall. It is never words on limewash, where it measures 1.49:1, and on its own wall the action turns ink.

rules.name: The Own Sign Rule
rules.body: A listing's colours stay on its own shopfront, its sign plates and its paints, and every word on a board takes that listing's lettering colour: through `[data-ground="brand"]` on a sign plate, and as the outline's fill on a painted board. The platform must not compete with what it sells, and each board is one measured pair.

rules.name: The Roles Not Values Rule
rules.body: A ground changes roles inside a scope; a `--palette-*` value is never redefined. A corrected sample then changes the palette and nothing else.

rules.name: The Painted Sign Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed speaks what is painted on a sign: a heading, a plaque, a price, the mark's name. Every sentence is Geist, so the condensed capitals keep their one meaning.

rules.name: The One Slant Rule
rules.body: The slant belongs to `heading-1`, once, on the home page's first screen; the coral shade belongs to that headline and to the tagline. It is the brand's one italic device, set in a face with a true italic, and coral is never words (3.09:1 on dusk).

rules.name: The Named Style Rule
rules.body: Every piece of interface text takes one of the seventeen named styles: Geist at 400, 500 or 600, Barlow Condensed at 600 or 700, nothing under 12px. A size or a weight set loose is a decision nobody recorded; the first words on a wide screen and the lettering on a plate are the recorded exceptions.

rules.name: The Street First Rule
rules.body: The home page opens on the street: the shopfronts are in the first screen with the headline, beside it on a desk and under it on a phone, at 1440 by 900 and at 390 by 844. The businesses are the proof, so they come before any claim.

rules.name: The Roof Line Rule
rules.body: Where one section's ground gives way to another's, a lambrequin in the colour of the ground above hangs 16px onto the ground below, and no ruled line divides one section from the next. A change of section then reads as a roof line.

rules.name: The Words In The Sky Rule
rules.body: The first words stand in the painted sky: every line ends before the roofline, and every sentence ends above the sky's floor, where white would no longer read. Where they do not fit, the second route steps aside and then the headline steps down a size; no frame is moved and no scrim is laid for them. One painting then serves a screen of any shape.

rules.name: The Flat Interface Rule
rules.body: The interface casts no shadow, fills with no gradient and blurs nothing; an inset edge is a line. Depth is said by a change of ground or a hairline, and the only light on the page is the street's own: paint, a lamp's bloom, a doorway's lamplight.

rules.name: The Solid Over The Street Rule
rules.body: Whatever sits over a painting on the stage is solid: the header in `dusk-deep`, the walk's card and a stop's name in `enamel`, the cue and the strip the stop marks stand on in `dusk-deep`. Its words and marks then never depend on what the stage is showing behind them. The first words are the one exception: they take the sky, under The Words In The Sky Rule.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: Anything pressed that is a control is a full pill, at least 48px tall, or 44px for the small button, a chip and the walk's cue. One shape then always means "press here"; a plaque has corners and is never pressed.

rules.name: The Shopfront Rule
rules.body: A business is always shown as its shopfront: painted where a painting exists and drawn where none does, with its own lettering set on its board, the same on the stage, on the terrace, in the catalogue and at the head of its page. The shutter rolling is the brand's one movement.

rules.name: The Plaque Rule
rules.body: A plaque names what is fixed about a business or about the walk: a number, a status, a town, a stop. It is enamel with a limewash rim, it carries `caption-4` or the card's own words, and it is not a button.

rules.name: The One Filled Rule
rules.body: A group of actions has one filled button; the rest are quiet buttons or arrow links. A visitor is shown one thing to do at a time.

rules.name: The Words Not Colour Rule
rules.body: A status, a sample, an error and the current page are said in words or drawn as a mark, with an icon where one helps, and the palette has no error colour. The hardest visitor is on a phone in bright light.

rules.name: The Sample Rule
rules.body: A sample says so wherever it stands: a tag on its shutter in every painting, a plaque beside its name, "a placeholder" at its price, a note on its page; the form never offers it. A sample must never pass for an offer.

rules.name: The Shut Sample Rule
rules.body: A sample's shutter never moves: it has no shutter to raise, on hover, on focus or on its own page, and only a real business opens. What cannot be bought is not shown open.

rules.name: The Visible First Rule
rules.body: Every word is visible in the markup; only `html.can-animate` may hide or mute anything, and never below 3:1. A crawler, a visitor without script and a visitor who asked for less motion all get the whole page.

rules.name: The Shutter Curve Rule
rules.body: `ease-roll` belongs to a shutter rolling on a shopfront and to a heading rising out of its mask; everything else takes `ease-out`, and the stage follows the scroll. A roller shutter starts heavy and settles, and that one curve is the brand's own.

rules.name: The Hold Rule
rules.body: The stage rests at each stop for the first and last 22% of the way to the next, and under reduced motion it cuts. A visitor who stops scrolling then has a still picture to read beside.

rules.name: The Still First Rule
rules.body: A still of the stage is painted before the plates and stays wherever they cannot run; the moving stage is an addition to a page that is already complete. The stage is never empty.

rules.name: The Blank Paint Rule
rules.body: A painting is made with every board, plaque, screen and paper blank, and what is true is set over the paint in code, from the data: a listing's lettering, its town, its number, a sample's tag. A picture can then never say something the data does not, and what the data cannot say stays blank.

rules.name: The Same Outline Rule
rules.body: A listing's lettering is one outline, drawn by `npm run wordmarks`, and every painted board, the document's cover, the sign plates and the drawn stand-in all draw it. A sign and its page cannot disagree.

rules.name: The Illustration Rule
rules.body: A generated picture is never passed for premises. Every plate, crop and still has a record beside it that names what made it, and the footer of every page says the shopfronts are illustrations and that a business comes without premises.

dos: Do fill one action in a group with `primary` #f8c618, set its label in `on-primary` #0a1639 (11.02:1), and put a quiet button or an arrow link beside it (The One Saffron Rule, The One Filled Rule).
Do keep a listing's colours on its shopfront, its sign plates and its paints, and set every word on a board in that listing's lettering colour (The Own Sign Rule).
Do change a ground by redefining roles in a scope, as `[data-ground="saffron"]` does, and leave every `--palette-*` value alone (The Roles Not Values Rule).
Do set a heading, a plaque and a price in Barlow Condensed capitals by `text-transform`, and every sentence in Geist (The Painted Sign Rule).
Do keep the slant for `heading-1` on the home page's first screen, and the coral shade for that headline and the tagline (The One Slant Rule).
Do give every piece of interface text one of the seventeen named styles (The Named Style Rule).
Do keep the shopfronts in the first screen of the home page, with the headline (The Street First Rule).
Do hang a lambrequin in the colour of the ground above it where two grounds meet (The Roof Line Rule).

Do keep the first words above the painted roofline and their sentences above the sky's floor, by shaping and fitting them, and measure them on the sky at the sizes they are shown (The Words In The Sky Rule).

Do separate one part of a page from the next with a ground or a hairline, and put anything else that sits over a painting on a solid ground of its own (The Flat Interface Rule, The Solid Over The Street Rule).
Do round anything pressed that is a control to a full pill, at least 48px tall, or 44px for the small button, a chip and the cue (The Pill Rule).
Do show a business as its shopfront, from `Shopfront.tsx` and the data, and name what is fixed about it on a plaque in `enamel` #0b2b8e with a limewash rim (The Shopfront Rule, The Plaque Rule).

Do say a status, a sample, an error and the current page in words or as a mark, mark a sample on its shutter, beside its name and at its price, and leave its shutter down (The Words Not Colour Rule, The Sample Rule, The Shut Sample Rule).

Do leave every word visible in the markup, roll a shopfront's shutter and a masked heading on `ease-roll`, rest the stage at each stop, and give each new movement its row under "Reduced motion and no script" (The Visible First Rule, The Shutter Curve Rule, The Hold Rule).

Do capture a still of the stage after any change to it, paint a new picture with every board, plaque, screen and paper blank, and set a listing's one outline over the paint from the data (The Still First Rule, The Blank Paint Rule, The Same Outline Rule).
Do save a generated picture's prompt and its record beside it, and keep the footer's line that says the shopfronts are illustrations (The Illustration Rule).
donts: Don't set words in saffron on limewash or fill a second button in a group: saffron on limewash measures 1.49:1 (The One Saffron Rule, The One Filled Rule).
Don't put the platform's ink, a grey or another listing's colour on a listing's board, or borrow a listing's colour for the platform (The Own Sign Rule).
Don't redefine a palette value inside a scope, or paint with a raw hex or one of Tailwind's colours: those are switched off and paint nothing (The Roles Not Values Rule).
Don't set a sentence in Barlow Condensed or type capitals into the markup: the capitals are `text-transform` (The Painted Sign Rule).
Don't slant a second heading, shade a third line, or set words in coral: it measures 3.09:1 on dusk (The One Slant Rule).
Don't set a loose size or weight, a weight over 700 or interface text under 12px (The Named Style Rule).
Don't open the home page with a claim, a picture of something else or a band of logos ahead of the street: the businesses are the proof (The Street First Rule).
Don't rule a line between two sections or hang a fringe in a colour that is not the ground above it (The Roof Line Rule).
Don't let a line of the first words run onto a roof or a sentence end on the afterglow, and never move a view or lay a scrim to make room for them (The Words In The Sky Rule).
Don't cast a soft shadow, fill with a gradient or blur a ground in the interface, and never lay a blur or a scrim over a painting (The Flat Interface Rule, The Solid Over The Street Rule).
Don't square a button or a chip, round a plaque into a pill, or make a plaque a button (The Pill Rule, The Plaque Rule).
Don't show a business as a photograph, a logo tile or a boxed card: it is a shopfront (The Shopfront Rule).

Don't mark a sample, a status or an error by colour alone, add an error colour, let a sample's price stand without "a placeholder", or raise a sample's shutter (The Words Not Colour Rule, The Sample Rule, The Shut Sample Rule).

Don't start anything hidden without `html.can-animate`, mute the tagline below 0.5 of the ink (3.77:1), loop a movement, or move the stage while a visitor rests at a stop (The Visible First Rule, The Shutter Curve Rule, The Hold Rule).

Don't leave the stage empty while the plates arrive, generate a picture with lettering in it, letter a board by hand or write on a painting what the data does not hold (The Still First Rule, The Blank Paint Rule, The Same Outline Rule).
Don't ship a generated picture without its record, call a painting a photograph, or let a shopfront pass for premises (The Illustration Rule).
